newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia plans aid for electricity industry.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia plans aid for electricity industry.

text.p: The Slovenian government said on Tuesday it plans to help out the country's electricity producers and distributors weather the current supply crisis by way of state capital injections and tax reductions.
Last week, Slovenia suffered its most acute lack of electricity since independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991 due to a breakdown at part of the Sostanj power plant.

Boris Sovic, state secretary of energy at the Ministry of Economic Affairs, said the country's electricity supply system was in need of extensive reconstruction, adding that to this end investment will rise to 27 billion tolars ($204.5 million) in 1996 from 15.5 billion in 1995.
This should increase further to 54.5 billion tolars in 1997 and to 66.9 billion in 1998, he said.
"My ministry also supports a demand to lift electricity prices by 9.7 percent, but I cannot predict the government's attitude towards this issue," he told a news conference.
Sovic said Slovenia's electricity supply problems could also be traced to debts incurred since 1974, as debt pay-backs limited the scope for investment.
In 1996, electricity companies will have to spend 15.2 billion tolars on debt repayments, up from 11.9 billion tolars in 1995.
Slovenia, which uses some 26 million kiloWatts of electricity a day, imports about 10 percent of its electricity consumed.
